transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm maya from redwood, this is liam our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:08] Elena: good thanks, bit of a busy week but we can go through this. we are evaluating options for low-latency model inferencing but security is the gating factor.
[00:20] Liam: cool, before we dive can i ask about your current stack and what your security must-haves are?
[00:30] Marcus: sure. we run most infra in GCP us-east1, use okta for sso, keys in cloud-kms, but for some regulated workloads we need hsm-backed keys and strict audit trails. we're also constrained on retention windows in eu for some customers.
[00:45] Priya: and from security side we need SOC2 or equivalent, ISO27001 would be nice but SOC2 is must, plus detailed audit logs per request for at least 1 year, preferably 3 for some clients. also need RBAC so only certain teams can call production models.
[01:05] Maya: totally makes sense. we commonly see that. redwood offers hosted, dedicated and private. hosted is quickest but you get shared control plane; we do SOC2 and publish certs, you can opt into managed KMS or BYOK for some tiers. dedicated gives dedicated GPU pools and stricter isolation, and private is a VPC/on-prem deployment where you control KMS and network.
[01:30] Elena: ok, two quick questions: can we BYOK and have an HSM be the root of trust? and how granular is RBAC?
[01:40] Liam: short answer: yes for private (and for dedicated with enterprise add-on we can support BYOK backed by HSM integration). RBAC is role-based and resource-scoped — teams, service accounts, token-level scoping, and route-level policies. there are some UI and api controls; we can lock down model versions and limit who can start rollout.
[01:58] Marcus: what about audit logs — do we get per-request token and model id, latency, response metadata? and can logs be shipped to our SIEM?
[02:08] Maya: yes, we emit rich audit logs containing request id, token id (or masked token), model id and variant, timestamps, latency, and error codes. for private we can push logs to your syslog or cloud logging; for hosted we provide a stream to your cloud account via a secure connector and support S3/BigQuery exports.
[02:30] Priya: retention — we need WORM-style retention for specific datasets for 3 years. can redwood support immutable storage or export for long-term archiving?
[02:42] Liam: we don't provide WORM in hosted by default, but for customers who need immutable retention we recommend private deployment with your storage backed by vendor or cloud's object lock, or using dedicated with an export workflow to your archive. we can also build a managed export to GCS with object lock flagged.
[03:05] Elena: how about SSO? we run okta, SCIM, we want user provisioning and SAML for single sign-on, plus audit of admin actions.
[03:15] Maya: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; for enterprise accounts we integrate with your IdP, and you can map groups to RBAC roles. admin actions are logged and accessible through audit exports.
[03:30] Marcus: service-to-service calls — we need mTLS or mutual auth between our apps and the redwood endpoints. can you do client certs?
[03:38] Liam: hosted supports token-based auth and mTLS at higher tiers; private gives you full control so you can enforce mutual TLS inside your VPC. for hosted we can set up API gateway with client certs when required.
[03:55] Priya: any certifications or pen-test reports we can review?
[04:00] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II report and ISO overview redacted artifacts, and pen test summary. i'll add links in the follow-up.
[04:10] Elena: great. cost-wise — we worry about latency vs cost; dedicated helps but is more expensive. what's the fallback if capacity spikes?
[04:20] Liam: we do smart routing and fallback to model variants; dedicated has burst to hosted for overflow if you enable it — all controlled by policy. performance profiles are published per model so you can estimate token cost.
[04:35] Marcus: do you do encryption at rest by default? what about key rotation and audits?
[04:40] Maya: yes encryption at rest is default; keys are customer-managed for private, and for hosted you can choose managed KMS or BYOK for eligible plans. key rotation is supported and we surface rotation events in audit logs.
[04:55] Priya: regulatory note: some datasets can't leave eu territory. can private be deployed in our eu region?
[05:03] Liam: absolutely — private supports VPC-deployed control plane within your cloud region; we can run the inference nodes in region and lock egress. for hosted, we have region-specific endpoints but some metadata might be in our control plane region — we can dig into specifics in follow-up.
[05:25] Elena: ok i want a couple of scenarios: (1) quick PoC on hosted to validate latency, (2) a security-grade pilot in dedicated with BYOK, or (3) full private if compliance requires. what do you recommend?
[05:40] Liam: i'd do hosted PoC to validate integration and metrics quickly, parallel track a dedicated pilot scoping to prove BYOK and audit, and if compliance gates are strict then move to private. we'll size the dedicated GPU pool for your throughput and test failover.
[06:00] Marcus: last technical ask — can we have per-tenant isolation within dedicated? we may want multiple projects separated.
[06:08] Liam: yes you can use tenant scoping, and token scoping per project; namespaces map to roles and models. we'll show a demo of that.
[06:20] Maya: okay, sounds like we have clear next steps. i'll share SOC2 and pen test artifacts, liam will draft architecture for BYOK/HSM, and priya will send retention constraints. any other questions?
[06:30] Priya: nothing else from me, thanks.
[06:33] Elena: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[06:35] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with links and schedule the scoping session. bye.
